name: The Village of Barovia, laid out from the E01 kit
frame: x east, y north, z up, in centimetres; v2 metres times 100; modules turned by quarter turns about their pivots (anticlockwise seen from above), then moved to at_cm
source: dungine.v2's village (Assets/Game/Scripts/Campaign/AreaVillage.cs), drawn from the book's map

buildings.label: the tall narrow townhouse
buildings.what: the tall narrow townhouse, 3 x 6 m

reserved.label: reserved plot
reserved.note: built elsewhere; nothing of the kit stands on it

roads.name: the high street and the west road

terrain.note: for the terrain batch (E02): the church stands on a low rise, 1.6 m at its middle, easing out from 12 to 26 m round it (as v2); the rest is the valley floor, the roads mud

ground.note: the ground is laid from the terrain kit (E02): the church on its rise (1.5 m), the manor on its hill (3 m; Peter: "put the manor on a hill"), the roads mud, the woods climbing round it all; every placement here stands on it (lift_cm: how far it was raised)

game_note: game export (game_export.py): each placement's glb is a path under pixel3d/export/game; place it at position_m (glTF metres: x east, y up, z south) turned by yaw_deg about +Y (rotation: the same as a glTF quaternion x y z w). The village's triangles at each LOD are in lod_triangles.
far_note: far meshes: one per building (and per 24 m tile of the open site), the modules merged at 15 cm in village coordinates; far away, draw it instead of the placements it lists
